{{Quote|It's a small price to pay for saving the galaxy.|Walex Blissex|<ref name="cocc">[[Crisis on Cloud City (adventure book)|''Crisis on Cloud City'']]</ref>}}
'''Walex Blissex''' was a [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] and [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] of [[Starship/Legends|starship]] design, and later a [[General/Legends|general]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], esteemed and respected throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. His designs ranged from mammoth [[Warship/Legends|warships]] to minuscule [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], and his clients ranged from [[Galaxy/Legends|pan-galactic]] governments to insurrectionist rebellion movements. Working for such [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] as [[Kuat Systems Engineering/Legends|Kuat Systems Engineering]] and [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]], Blissex created mainstays of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], such as the [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], and the [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]]. Blissex himself was not at ease with creating craft that could and would be used as killing machines, but he consoled himself with the fact that they were being used to police the galaxy and keep others from harm. Unable to use a [[Computer/Legends|computer]] properly, Blissex relied on assistants and his daughter, [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira]]. When [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] made his grab for unlimited power in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Blissex rejected his [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] and quietly became a founding member of the Alliance to Restore the Republic.

Lira, however, had other ideas, and essentially took her father's role in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Despite this, she was not as talented as her father, and when the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] broke out twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, the domestic dispute between Blissex and Lira became intertwined with galactic affairs. The two would tangle throughout the war, with Lira consistently trying to trap or murder her father. Blissex overcame all obstacles however, and was able to serve the Alliance faithfully until it became the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. In his later years, Blissex would see less active duty, but would serve with [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna's]] "[[Gray Cadre/Legends|Gray Cadre]]" and eventually design the [[Republic-class Star Destroyer|''Republic''-class Star Destroyer]].

==Biography==
===Galactic Republic===
====The Clone Wars====
{{Quote|She is a remarkable vessel. With the engineering breakthroughs we tackled developing her, she's just the start. She's a real sign of things to come.|Walex Blissex|<ref name="hnn">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|jediwatch/13314_1.html|New Jedi Starfighter Unveiled}}</ref>}}
[[File:Walex_and_Lira_Blissex.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Walex and Lira Blissex contemplate a new design.]]
Walex Blissex was a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] who designed all kinds of craft, from [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] to [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]]. At some stage in his career, he earned the title of [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]].<ref name="sf">[[Starfall (adventure)|''Starfall'']]</ref> One of his personal friends was [[Shil Tervo/Legends|Shil Tervo]], who he occasionally collaborated with.<ref name="ss">''[[Stock Ships]]''</ref> Due to his inability to operate a computer, Blissex was always aided by assistants and his daughter, [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira]].<ref name="ff130">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 130|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 130]]</ref> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Blissex was working at [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], with the title of [[Project Engineer]].<ref name="hnn" /> Inspired by the [[Aurek-class tactical strikefighter|''Aurek''-class tactical strikefighters]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]],<ref name="egtw">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> he designed and developed the [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], a small craft purpose-built for use by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Blissex was proud of his craft, and joined in the unveiling on [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] with [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Risi Lenoan]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] and [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]]. Blissex took this opportunity to speak to [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].<ref name="hnn" />

Blissex would adopt a number of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] modifications when designing the [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], which added a standard [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] port forward of the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]]. Blissex's next design was the [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptor]], a bold new direction in starcraft design. That new design was a fast, agile craft intended to be an extension of a Jedi [[Pilot/Legends|pilot's]] abilities and reliant on their [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-enhanced senses. Lacking [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]], and with its [[Armor/Legends|armor]], [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], and systems stripped down, the Eta-2 allowed its Jedi pilots to fly almost as fast as they could think.<ref name="egtw" />

As Kuat Drive Yards' top shipwright, Blissex was alarmed by [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] rush to war, and disturbed by the machinations of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] war ministers and their ties to Kuat Drive Yards. [[Arch-Provost/Legends|Arch-Provost]] [[Bengila Urlan]] lured away Blissex to work for StarDrive, and thought he had crippled Kuat Drive Yards. However the Republic already depended on the company's shipyards, [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] routes, and specialist [[Deepdock/Legends|deepdocks]] designed for new classes of massive [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], and Lira was also employed by Kuat Drive Yards.<ref name="egtw" />

In the waning days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Blissex, with the help of [[Bevel Lemelisk]],<ref name="negtc">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> designed the [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]] for [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]]. The craft was considered to be among the best of its kind, and although it saw limited use by the Republic, it would be a mainstay of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] fleet in the future.<ref name="is" /> Although the ''Victory''-class cruisers were originally designed to operate [[NTB-630 naval bomber/Legends|NTB-630 Naval Bombers]] alongside short-range [[A-6 Interceptor]]s, their capacity was largely given over to [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighters]] by the end, and Blissex worked on developing a new generation of [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] and [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing starfighters]] designed to [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]] on equal terms with any starfighters in [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="egtw" /> Around the same time of designing the ''Victory''-class Destroyers, Blissex also created the initial design for the [[Gladiator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Gladiator''-class Star Destroyer]], envisioning it as an escort for the ''Victory''-class.<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

Blissex himself was never comfortable with devising war machines, but he acknowledged the need for them to keep the peace.<ref name="ff121" /> During this time, Blissex was called upon by the [[Kuat Systems Engineering/Legends|Kuat Systems Engineering]] once more to develop the [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter]], as a replacement for the [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent]]. Blissex saw this as an opportunity to correct flaws he perceived in the Delta-7.<ref name="dbvw">{{DB|starship|vwingstarfighter|V-wing starfighter}}</ref>

====Defection and heartbreak====
When [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] made his grab for power in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Blissex chose to disappear from the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] spotlight. He was idealistic, and he vehemently disagreed with Palpatine's policy of using weapons of mass destruction to police his new Galactic Empire, but he understood the threat that the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] posed to his safety. Rather than be forced to do that which he believed wrong, Blissex became one of the founding members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Despite this, his daughter married [[Governor/Legends|Imperial Governor]] [[Denn Wessex]] of the [[Relgim sector/Legends|Relgim sector]] and took her father's intended place in the Empire. She designed the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]], working from her father's designs for the ''Victory I''-class.<ref name="ff121" />

===The Rebel Alliance===
[[File:General_Walex_Blissex_RaR.png|thumb|right|250px|Blissex works on the design of the RZ-1 A-wing starfighter.]]
{{Quote|Develop technology without wisdom or prudence and your servant shall become your executioner.|Walex Blissex|<ref name="egtw" />}}
====The A-wing====
Following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] realized that the Alliance needed a starfighter that could match the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] for speed and maneuverability. He approached Blissex, and together they developed the [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]].<ref name="ras">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> Blissex once more used the design of the Old Republic's Aurek strikefighters as the inspiration.<ref name="egtw" /> Though [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] was initially skeptical, she gave in to the now-popular Dodonna, and the craft was developed.<ref name="ras" /> For research, Blissex and Dodonna examined the sleek ships of the [[Tammuz-an space navy]], such as the [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearhead]].<ref name="dbaw">{{DB|starship|awingstarfighter|A-wing starfighter}}</ref> Mothma, however, refused to adequately fund the project, forcing Blissex to get the maximum output for the lowest amount of input. Putting his skills to good use, Blissex was able to successfully assemble the RZ-1, using components so common that they could be found anywhere in the galaxy, without sacrificing any performance whatsoever.<ref name="ras" /> Due to his service to the Alliance, he was given the honorary rank of general.<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=General Walex Blissex}}</ref>

====Reunion on the ''Subjugator''====
{{Quote|No one knows the working of this ship better than I do.|Walex Blissex, on the ''Victory''-class Star Destroyer|<ref name="sf" />}}
Blissex served the Alliance faithfully as an engineering advisor, but the inconsolable rift between him and his daughter affected him greatly. Although he intended to amend their relationship, Lira did not. Eventually, Blissex learned from Denn Wessex that his daughter was apparently dying. Wessex pleaded with Blissex to make the trip to the Relgim sector to see Lira, but [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] was skeptical. Labeling it a trap, they cautioned Blissex against making the journey, but the esteemed engineer insisted that he was of no use to the Empire and that he would make the trip no matter what.<ref name="ff121" /><ref name="Note">The events depicted here occur in the roleplaying game [[Starfall (adventure)|''Starfall'']]. As such, some of the particular events, and the number and identify of the characters involved were left open. Some illustrations were provided, which indicated the Rebel group was composed of a [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] and three Humans; two female and one male. However, in retelling the events of this adventure, ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'' described and named just two Rebel agents, Rexellian Marshall and Kan Deans. The effect of this appears to be to limit the canonical number of player characters in the adventure to two.</ref>

Alliance High Command was still not satisfied, and so General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]] dispatched two of his agents, [[Rexellian Marshall]] and [[Kan Deans]] to watch over Blissex. Wessex arranged to have Blissex picked up from [[Kwenn Space Station/Legends|Kwenn Space Station]] by the ''Victory''-class Star Destroyer [[Subjugator (Victory-class)|''Subjugator'']], which would be traveling under the ruse of a supply stop. Upon reaching Kwenn, Blissex, Marshall and Deans were all thrown in the ''Subjugator''{{'s}} detention cells, ready for interrogation by the fit and well Lira Wessex. Lira had devised the trap, as her designs for the ''Imperial-I''-class had never been able to match the quality they would have reached at her father's hands.<ref name="ff121" />

During the interrogation, the ''Subjugator'' fell under attack from [[Task Force Starfall]], who was unaware that Blissex was aboard. During the battle, the Star Destroyer and the Rebel command ship took heavy damage, but the ''Subjugator'' was crippled, causing [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Kolaff]] to set the ''Subjugator'' to self-destruct just as the Rebels would make their second attack, using a code known only to Lira and Blissex. During a power blackout, Marshall and Deans liberated Blissex from an interrogation droid.<ref name="ff130" /> Due to the rigorous interrogation, the aging Blissex was exhausted and barely able to stand.<ref name="sf" /> The trio then made their way through the burning body of the ''Subjugator'' while being antagonized by Kolaff. Blissex's knowledge of his own ship design was critical in guiding the small group through the ship, but his comrades soon discovered that he did not know how to operate a computer. Deans, however, was able to discover Kolaff's plan to destroy the ship.<ref name="ff130" />

[[File:OriginalBlissex-SF.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Walex Blissex during the ''Subjugator'' incident]]
Blissex realized he could turn the tables on Kolaff by setting the ship to self-destruct an hour earlier than scheduled. Making their way to the ship's core, Blissex, Marshall, and Deans battled various Imperial troopers along the way. Upon reaching the core, Blissex noticed that the self-destruct sequence was one known only to him and one other person: his daughter. The truth of the situation dawned on Blissex, and he realized that his own daughter had trapped him.<ref name="sf" /> The engineer was devastated at the news, but was given little time to console himself.<ref name="ff130" />

The gambit to alter the self-destruct sequence proved to be another trap, and the trio found themselves battling stormtroopers once again. Learning of an unoccupied shuttle in a far-off landing bay, the group set off throughout the harried ship, with Blissex guiding his two allies every step of the way. Eventually, the group encountered [[T-3PO (Subjugator)|T-3PO]], a protocol droid capable of communicating with the ship's defense mechanisms. Seeing that the droid would come in useful, the Rebels decided to allow it to tag along. Traversing through areas of the ship so damaged that the artificial gravity had lapsed, the group eventually found their way to the docking bays, only to be confronted by Kolaff in an [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-ST]].<ref name="sf" />

Marshall and Deans were able to procure their own AT-ST and defeated Kolaff in a brief confrontation, and the Rebels then moved on to Hangar Bay G-12.<ref name="sf" /> However, Lira and a squad of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] arrived to stop Blissex and his allies from escaping. As the assailants attempted to kill the Rebels, the droid complement of the ''Subjugator'', abandoned by their masters, attacked Lira and the stormtroopers, buying Blissex time to escape. The members of Task Force Starfall picked up the trio, and Lira too was able to depart before the ''Subjugator'' exploded. Despite this, Blissex assumed that Lira had died in the explosion, leaving him no opportunity to reconcile their relationship. Heartbroken, Blissex returned to active service.<ref name="ff130" />

====Wayward experiments====
{{Quote|Father, what a pleasant surprise. I thought you were no longer interested in building battle platforms.''"<br />"''I didn't know you had an interest in killing innocent scientists.|Lira Wessex and Walex Blissex|<ref name="cocc" />}}
Sometime later, Blissex received a holographic message from his friend, Doctor [[Issan Len]]. Len had developed the [[X0-X1]], a droid that could control multi-faceted systems by itself. The doctor called Blissex in to inspect the new droid, but he also requested that Blissex arrange Alliance protection for the machine, as it would be deadly in the Empire's hands. However, by the time Blissex arrived at [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], it was too late. He and his escort were delayed by some hostile droids, but as they reached Dr. Len's office, they discovered that he had been recently murdered and the X0-X1 prototype had been stolen.<ref name="cocc" />

Investigating the crime scene, the Rebels deduced that Len had been murdered by [[F-3PO]], a protocol droid from [[Bioniip Laboratories/Legends|Bioniip Laboratories]]. The droid, however, had no recollection of the incident, and only spoke of "black tentacles" reaching out towards him. Before Blissex and his guards could act on the information, [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] arrived on the scene with a detachment of his guards. He insisted that the Rebels solve the crime or be arrested as suspects in Len's death. Following their only lead, the Rebels traveled to Bioniip Laboratories.<ref name="cocc" />

[[File:CrazyBlissex-CoCC.png|thumb|right|Blissex during the Cloud City incident]]
Taking F-3PO with them, the Rebels were informed by the Bioniip receptionist that the protocol droid had been sold to none other than Lira Wessex. Instead of expressing surprise at the discovery, Blissex was only disappointed, and to think that his daughter might have been involved in Len's death affected him greatly. F-3PO, at first struggling to remember Lira, suddenly piped up and mentioned that his master was going to meet one Doctor [[Vreen]] at the [[Royal Casino/Legends|Royal Casino]]. Hastily traveling to the Casino, the Rebels met a disguised Calrissian at a [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] table. Calrissian had seen someone matching Lira's description, but he requested that one of the Rebels play a game of sabacc with him. As the game started, the group was approached by [[Helm Iskraker]], who was also there to meet Vreen.<ref name="cocc" />

During the game, they learned from Iskraker that he had stolen seven key cards from [[SecuriCo]] in the [[Indellian system/Legends|Indellum system]], though when probed for the identity of his client, the alien feigned ignorance. He also had no knowledge of Lira whatsoever. Lira herself eventually showed up and sat down at the sabacc table with Iskraker, Blissex, the Rebels, and the disguised Calrissian. After some verbal sparring between Blissex and his daughter, Lira inquired as to Vreen's whereabouts, but no one had any answers. Lira was also puzzled by the accusation that F-3PO was her droid, as she had never owned a protocol droid in her life.<ref name="cocc" />

As the sabacc game progressed, the cards evolved into dark, flat, hemispherical shapes with tentacles coming out of them. The evolved cards matched the description recalled by F-3PO at Len's lab. At that moment, a large labor droid entered the casino and moved to attack the patrons. After Blissex's Rebel escorts defeated the droid, however, they discovered that Lira, Iskraker, and Calrissian had all left. With information extracted from the wayward labor droid, the Rebels learned that it had come from Bioniip, which was apparently where Vreen was located.<ref name="cocc" />

====Blackout====
Returning to Bioniip Labs, the Rebels were met with heavy resistance from a variety of droids. Left with no alternative, they blasted their way into the facility. They were confronted by odd humanoid droids and eventually discovered that the Bioniip cafeteria was been used as a makeshift prison. The Bioniip staff were being held there by the droids, who had apparently taken over the labs. They informed Blissex and his escorts that Vreen was alive and had hand-picked several scientists at gunpoint several hours prior. Venturing further into the facility, the Rebels came across a group of scientist's bodies that had been somehow made half machine. One of the bodies, situated on a lab table, was that of the still-alive Dr. Vreen.<ref name="cocc" />

As the half-mechanical Vreen awoke, Blissex and his allies confronted him. They learned that he had taken X0-X1 somewhere, but the exact location was lost to him. What he did know was that the location was sealed with seven locks, and that these locks could only be opened with the help of a "gold-skinned alien" and a "black haired woman." Though the Rebels realized that the alien was Iskraker, they had no clues as to the identity of the woman. Vreen had been tortured by X0-X1 and was forced to create [[Evolution Droid]]s&mdash;microscopic units that could transform flesh into metal. The scientists he had experimented on were dead, so he had been forced to use himself as a test subject. The only other things Vreen could remember were that some droids had taken a canister of Evolution Droids out of the lab, and that X0-X1 was somehow controlling all the droids.<ref name="cocc" />

Pressing Vreen further, the Rebels learned that the black haired woman was [[Bellum]] the [[Forger]]. They also discovered that X0-X1 planned to take over Cloud City entirely. As the group discussed the situation with Vreen, X0-X1 sent in a mouse droid carrying the evolution virus, hoping to infect Blissex and his companions. The plot was foiled however, and Blissex realized that the virus could be reversed to effect droids. Working quickly with Vreen, he developed a batch that would effectively serve as a poison to X0-X1.<ref name="cocc" />

[[File:WalexBlissex-FF121.png|thumb|left|150px|Walex Blissex in his Alliance Command uniform]]
Before the Rebels were given a chance to depart Bioniip Laboratories, Cloud City experienced a total blackout. The previously imprisoned scientists helped Blissex and his team stock up on supplies before setting out for [[Bellum's Keys & Copies|Bellum's shop]], with Vreen in tow. On the way, they encountered several droids installing canisters full of the Evolution virus in the air vents, with approximately two hours until activation. Realizing that time was of the essence, the group hurriedly made their way to Bellum's shop. Meeting with Bellum, they asked her about Vreen and the keys he had commissioned for the seven locks that would guide them to X0-X1. Although the Forger didn't have the spare keys, she did know that one of them was for a maintenance corridor near [[K'cri's Cafe]]. Bellum, however, did not have the keys themselves, as they had been stolen from her earlier.<ref name="cocc" />

However, Vreen realized that they could find X0-X1 by using the serial numbers on the keys. The group searched Bellum's shop for clues as to who might have stolen the [[cold box]] containing Bellum's copies and found some gold flakes, left by Iskraker's alien skin. Before the Rebels could track down the thief, Bellum was cut down by the fire of one of X0-X1's droids. After defeating the droid, Blissex and his allies realized that they would not be able to locate Iskraker, as only Bellum had known his location. Fortunately for them, they soon chanced upon [[Widget (organic)|Widget]], a friend of Iskraker's. After some trickery and convincing, the Rebels were able to get Widget to lead them to Iskraker's ship, the ''[[Erratic Orbit]]''.<ref name="cocc" />

Catching up to Iskraker at [[hangar bay 487B]], Blissex and his companions arrived to see the alien giving Lira Wessex the cold box. Some mercenaries working for Lira engaged the Rebels, giving Blissex's daughter a chance to escape. The Rebels overcame the distraction, and hunted the Imperial engineer down. Lira, who had recently had [[Cyborg/Legends|cybernetic implants]] installed, scanned the cold box for the key's serial number as she fled from her father and his men. During the chase, however, Lira was knocked off a ledge and was forced to request aid from the Rebels. Turning the tables on them, she threw the cold box away into Bespin's clouds, forcing Blissex and the Rebels to save her for her memory.<ref name="cocc" />

====Foiling X0-X1====
{{Quote|Dr. Blissex, you of all people should recognize the value redesigning and rebuilding.''"<br />"''Agreed. But is it truly efficient to waste thousands of productive lives?|X0-X1 and Walex Blissex|<ref name="cocc" />}}
Traveling to K'cri's Cafe, Lira explained that Dr. Vreen had contacted her and informed her of X0-X1, which could be used to build weapons platforms by itself, as it was doing to Cloud City as they spoke. The Rebels the first lock, then progressed through all seven, battling all manner of traps and adversaries thrown at them by X0-X1. Reaching the Cloud City computer core where X0-X1 resided, the group were confronted by Vreen, who had completed his transformation process and was now completely and utterly mechanical. He attempted to acquire Blissex's droid poison, but was destroyed by the Rebels. Despite this, they were unable to reach X0-X1, as the droid had a number of security measures in place protecting itself.<ref name="cocc" />

Blissex realized that the only way to destroy X0-X1 was to deactivate Cloud City's computer core. However, the core regulated Cloud City's generators, allowing it to float, and deactivating the core would cause the city to plummet for thirty seconds before being crumpled by Bespin's pressure. Blissex realized this, but insisted it was the only hope for the city. If the Rebels could destroy the droid within the thirty second time frame, the core could be re-activated, allowing the city to float once more. The Rebels executed the plan and were able to pull it off successfully, destroying X0-X1. Lira, however, took the opportunity to turn the tables once more on her father. Holding a blaster to Blissex's head, she gloated while a group of thugs she had hired to watch over her entered the room. However, Calrissian had been hiding in the core room the whole time with a detachment of his guards, and he chose that moment to reveal himself. Requesting that Lira leave the city, he dropped the murder allegations against Blissex and his men and thanked them for their services to Cloud City.<ref name="cocc" />

====Battle of Endor and the New Republic====
[[File:BlissexBriefing-FF130.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Walex Blissex (right) attends the Battle of Endor briefing on the ''Home One'' in 4 ABY.]]
In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Blissex was present aboard the [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']], in preparation for the climactic [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="rotj">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Blissex's expertise in the field of Star Destroyers gave him particular call to be present for the battle, as the Alliance would face a large amount of them over the Sanctuary Moon. In particular, Blissex provided the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing]] pilots with calculations and recommendations that would lead them to destroy one Star Destroyer during the battle and damage several others. Ironically, one of Blissex's A-wing starfighters would destroy the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], which was designed by Lira.<ref name="ff130" /> The Endor briefing would prove to be one of the last times Blissex was seen in public.<ref name="ff121" />

Blissex eventually retired from active service. Several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, his friendship with Jan Dodonna would bring him back into the military fold. Blissex became a part of Dodonna's "[[Gray Cadre/Legends|Gray Cadre]]," which served as a council of military advisors to the [[New Republic High Command/Legends|New Republic High Command]].<ref name="ff130" /> Amongst the battle hardened veterans that made up the group, Blissex was the most quiet and reserved of the lot.<ref name="ff121" /> Blissex would later design the [[Republic-class Star Destroyer|''Republic''-class Star Destroyer]], an improvement and follow-up to his aging ''Victory''-class. Though not as large as Lira's ''Imperial''-class, it boasted 20 percent more firepower and only a fifth of the crew complement.<ref name="ctd">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Walex Blissex tended to see issues in black and white, and apart from his refusal to comply with Palpatine's new regime, he would generally abide by the law. He was particularly disappointed to see his creations, such as the ''Victory''-class Star Destroyer, turned into a symbol of terror by the Empire.<ref name="cocc" /> Despite this, Blissex was proud of his creations.<ref name="hnn" /> At heart, Blissex was a pacifist and idealist, which put him at odds with his daughter on several occasions.<ref name="sf" /> He chose not to speak out publicly against the reforms of 19 BBY; rather, he chose to act, which was considerably more dangerous.<ref name="ff121" /> As a pacifist, Blissex would again be disturbed at the New Republic's rush to conflict and the machinations of its war ministers.<ref name="egtw" />

Blissex faithfully served the Alliance, but he had one weakness: his daughter. The nonreciprocating love he had for her allowed Lira to lure him into a variety of traps and use him as leverage. Blissex was always hurt deeply by Lira's machinations, and even though she had attempted to kill him, he was still crestfallen at the prospect of her death on the ''Subjugator''.<ref name="ff130" /> When she resurfaced shortly afterwards on Cloud City, he was not surprised, but rather disappointed that she was still trying to outwit and destroy her father in the name of the Empire.<ref name="cocc" />
